items.statement: Orthogonal rotation carries the literal diagonal inverse-precision Gaussian exactly to the Gaussian target of the conjugated precision. (R_O)_\#N(0,\Lambda^{-1})=N\!\left(0,(O\Lambda O^\top)^{-1}\right),\qquad R_Oz=Oz. \(d\in\mathbb N\), \(d\ge2\), and \(\kappa\in\mathbb R\), \(\kappa\ge2\). This is the hard-family law auxiliary; the full lower-bound parameter regime is handled separately. For paper indices \(i=1,\ldots,d\), \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(\lambda_i=(\kappa+1)/2+(\kappa-1)\cos\theta_i/2\), and \(\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)\). Lean uses the same grid with zero-based Fin d indices. \(O\in O(d)\) is any fixed real orthogonal matrix, with either determinant sign; \(A=O\Lambda O^\top\). The claim is pointwise in this fixed basis, with no joint or conditional-law assertion for a random basis. \(\Lambda\) and \(A\) are precision matrices. Their matrix inverses are the covariances in the actual Gaussian constructors. Positive definiteness is supplied internally by the existing admissibility theorem, rather than by an added premise.

obligations.label: Actual orthogonal pushforward diagonal Gaussian equals the actual inverse-precision target; covariance facts derived internally.

bindings.boundary: This is the fixed-basis Gaussian law and the private target norm-moment component. It supplies no joint Haar or adaptive output law, full Lemma4.5, target test-probability bound, concentration-valid absolute constant, sampling algorithm, oracle/TV/precision/query-cap/cost adapter, or either complete main lower bound. The basis rotation is a mathematical coordinate map with no algorithmic access or cost claim.

assumption_deltas.reason: Orthogonality makes the two pointwise coordinate statements equivalent. No random-O joint kernel or conditional representative is asserted.
